lead_summary: UTHealth Houston reports a peptide (BLMP6) targeting fibulin-4 on metastatic triple-negative breast cancer cells. Fluorescent-dye conjugate localised to metastatic cells in mice; MMAE drug conjugate suppressed metastasis and improved survival in mice; AI modelling predicted binding to human fibulin-4; binding confirmed on human tissue arrays ex vivo.
why_valuable: Fills the one mechanism_vs_evidence slot within frozen biological scope, AND sits deliberately outside the existing mechanism cluster — all six current mechanism cases (013, 024, 028, 030, 036, 044) are neuro/aging/mouse-memory. This is oncology, so it widens Shape A coverage without near-duplication.
candidate_forensic_shape: Preclinical mouse efficacy plus ex-vivo human tissue binding presented as demonstrating clinical translatability. Binding to human tissue is not evidence of therapeutic benefit in humans.

verified_so_far.republication_verified: ecancer news item 28181, dated 30 Apr 2026, which names its source as University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

BLOCKER: The UTHealth press release at https://www.uth.edu/news/story/preclinical-efficacy-of-experimental-peptide-therapy-suggests-a-new-target-for-metastatic-breast-cancer-treatments-uthealth-houston-researchers-find returned an EMPTY response (likely client-rendered). The claim source could not be read directly.
why_this_blocks_acceptance: The candidate forensic defect rests on one sentence: 'The team used AI to predict BLMP6 binding to human fibulin-4 and demonstrated that the results seen in mice could be translated clinically by confirming that BLMP6 targets human breast cancer cells.' This appears in the ecancer republication. It is UNRESOLVED whether that wording is UTHealth's or ecancer's editorial paraphrase. §11 forbids attributing a secondary outlet's wording to the originating institution, and §29 forbids accepting a candidate resting on an unverified paraphrase. The case CANNOT proceed on the ecancer text.
important_counter_observation: Much of the coverage is well hedged — the headline says 'Preclinical efficacy... suggests', the body says 'may open the door', and Kolonin's own quoted words explicitly scope to preclinical models: 'There is efficacy of both the BLMP6-drug conjugate and BLMP6-based imaging probes useful for metastasis detection that we demonstrated in preclinical cancer models.' If the unverified sentence turns out to be ecancer's, the UTHealth release may well be SOLID rather than mechanism_vs_evidence, and the forensic issue would shift to the republication layer instead. The label genuinely depends on resolving authorship.
next_step: Retrieve the UTHealth page via a JavaScript-rendering browser tool, or obtain the release from the institutional newsroom archive. Then open the Molecular Therapy Oncology paper to verify what was actually demonstrated in humans (binding only vs any clinical endpoint). Only then assign a candidate ID.
